cluster_name: Trump scales back US-South Korea drills seeking Kim Jong Un meeting
event_summary: Trump ordered the Pentagon to substantially reduce annual Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises with South Korea; North Korea responded by firing ballistic missiles and Trump announced plans to meet Kim Jong Un later in 2026.
tldr: Headlines collectively assert that Trump cut joint US-South Korea drills to court Kim Jong Un, but North Korea answered with a missile barrage rather than diplomacy. The security/deterrence framing dominates the headline layer — 'fires barrage,' 'launches missiles,' 'cuts short drills' — while a parallel diplomatic cluster frames the story as personal Trump-Kim outreach ('courts Kim,' 'makes overtures,' 'eyes talks'). South Korean outlets are the only ones whose headlines foreground the domestic political fracture the drill cut caused. The Atlantic stands alone in connecting the moves to Iran's nuclear calculus — a framing present only in opinion headlines, absent from straight news titles.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to connect the drill cuts to Iran nuclear signaling — framing that does not appear in any straight news title across the other 17 outlets.
Only headline to explicitly foreground China's strategic interest, using the word 'weakened' for Trump — a framing absent from US, South Korean, and Chinese state media headlines.
Most optimistic headline for Trump diplomacy ('Trump says he will meet Kim Jong-un this year') with no qualifier or caveat — sole outlet to omit Pyongyang's cool response from its title.

bottom_line: The headline layer advertises the story as a diplomatic gamble meeting provocative rebuff — Trump courts Kim, North Korea fires missiles — while largely burying in the body text the more consequential detail that Seoul learned of the exercise cut from a Trump social media post rather than diplomatic consultation.
